patients.summary: Thirty-four-year-old administrative coordinator with obesity and a remote gallstone history who joined in 2022. In 2025 a monochorionic monoamniotic twin pregnancy was complicated by gestational diabetes on insulin and complete placenta previa with two bleeds, ending at 30 weeks in demise of both twins and cesarean delivery; postpartum glucose testing was normal and she is back at work.

conditions.label: Cholelithiasis
conditions.note: remote history of gallstones; gallbladder in place, never operated, no current symptoms

social.value: Occasional; a glass of wine now and then

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
30-year-old woman joining the practice. Her primary care office of several years is closing its adult panel and she wanted a doctor she could reach directly.

No active complaints today. Main thing she wants to work on is weight. Says it has been about the same for the last few years, up from where it was in her twenties. Tries to cook at home most nights, but sits at a desk all day as an administrative coordinator and does not exercise on a schedule.

PMH: obesity. Had gallstones seen years ago, never had surgery, no attacks she can recall since; no pain after meals now.
PSH: none.
OB: G1P1001, one prior pregnancy without complications, vaginal delivery at term. Child is well.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother developed type 2 diabetes at 45. Maternal grandmother carried twins. No early heart disease she knows of.
Social: married, one child at home. Never smoked. Drinks rarely, a glass of wine here and there. No drug use.

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, abdominal pain, change in bowels, heavy or irregular periods, polyuria or polydipsia, mood complaints.

Exam: vitals as charted. BMI 32. Pleasant, in no distress. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular rate and rhythm without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen obese, soft, nontender, no organomegaly, no RUQ tenderness. Extremities without edema. Skin without acanthosis.

Assessment/plan:
1. Obesity, BMI 32. Talked through realistic targets: a 5 to 7 percent loss over a year, walking at lunch, protein at breakfast, fewer sweetened drinks. She would rather start on her own than see a program. Recheck in about 6 months.
2. Family history of diabetes and obesity: A1c today.
3. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screen, she agrees. Last Pap with HPV was 2021 at her old office per her report; will confirm from records. Flu shot and the fall COVID booster at a nurse visit next month since she wants to space them from today's draw.
4. Gallstone history: asymptomatic, nothing to do. Return if she has pain after meals.

Records release signed for her prior office. Follow up 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records request faxed to patient's prior primary care office with signed release. Requested last 3 years of notes, labs, immunizations and cervical screening results.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wanda, your blood work from Wednesday is all normal: blood count, kidney and liver tests, thyroid, cholesterol, and your A1c is in the normal range, so no sign of diabetes. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative and don't need to be repeated unless something changes. We'll recheck the A1c yearly given your mom's history. See you for the shots next month.

events.reason: Records from prior primary care office

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Satisfactory for evaluation; endocervical/transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Records from Prior Primary Care Office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Received 41 pages from prior primary care office (notes 2019 to 2022). Abstracted:
- Problem list: obesity; history of cholelithiasis (no surgery).
- Medications: none.
- Allergies: NKDA.
- Immunizations: Tdap 05/2019; Pfizer COVID primary series 04/2021. Entered.
- Cervical screening: Pap with HPV co-test 06/2021, NILM, HPV negative. Next due 2026.
- Obstetric: one prior uncomplicated pregnancy, term vaginal delivery; prenatal care through an outside OB.
- Labs: annual CBC and metabolic panels normal.
Scanned to media. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for flu and bivalent COVID booster. Screening negative, not pregnant, no prior vaccine reactions. Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM right deltoid, COVID bivalent IM left deltoid. VIS provided. Waited 15 minutes without issue.

documents.title: Wellness Program Form
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, my job has a wellness program and they want a form signed by my doctor with my blood pressure, BMI and cholesterol from this year. Can I upload it here? Thank you!

documents.title: RE: Wellness Program Form
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Yes, please upload it under Documents. We'll fill it in from your September visit and labs and have the doctor sign. Allow 3 to 5 business days.

documents.title: No-Show
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Patient did not arrive for 3:00 follow-up. Called her mobile, she had a work deadline and forgot. Rebooked for 3/29.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Weight follow-up (rescheduled from the 8th).

She has been packing lunches and stopped the afternoon soda. Walking some evenings when the weather allows, maybe twice a week. Weight is within a pound or two of September, which she finds discouraging. Sleeping about 7 hours.

No meds. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted, BP normal. Well appearing. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P: Obesity, BMI 32, stable. Stable weight is not failure; the goal for the next stretch is adding structured activity, 150 minutes a week, and a food log for two weeks to see where the calories are. She is not interested in medication or a program right now, which is reasonable. Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Vaccine Record
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello, HR is asking for my vaccination record for our office file. Is there a way to print it from the portal or can you send it?

documents.title: RE: Vaccine Record
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Wanda, I've attached your immunization record as a PDF to this message. It includes the Tdap from 2019, your COVID shots and last fall's flu shot. You can also print it any time under Health > Immunizations.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 31 y/o.

Interval: doing well. Walking more over the summer, less now that it gets dark early. Weight up slightly from spring. No new symptoms. Periods regular. No GI complaints, nothing to suggest gallbladder trouble.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: unchanged; never smoker, rare alcohol.
FH: mother with type 2 DM (onset 45).

PHQ-2 0.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well, no distress. Thyroid normal size. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Breasts: declined today, no concerns. No edema. Skin normal.

A/P:
- Health maintenance: Pap/HPV last 2021, normal, not due until 2026. Flu shot given. COVID updated vaccine at her pharmacy when it arrives. Tdap current (2019).
- Obesity, BMI 32: same counseling as before; she'd like to try a step goal with a coworker. Offered nutrition referral, declines for now.
- Diabetes screening: A1c with CMP and lipids today.
Return in a year, or sooner.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Wanda, results from your physical look good. A1c remains normal, cholesterol panel is fine, and kidney and liver numbers are normal. Nothing to change. Keep at the walking.

documents.title: Pharmacy Immunization Notification
documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Immunization administered at community pharmacy: COVID-19 vaccine, 2023-2024 formula, 0.3 mL IM left deltoid, 11/02/2023. Patient tolerated without incident.
